haiku-low.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction commits, then the row is safe-copied to PG with a 500 ms timeout. A PG failure or timeout does not fail the request; the outbox row stays for repair.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the stored one, and the id is not in that DB's users_tombstones.
haiku-low.q3: Every instance must be confirmed on dual_mysql_primary, then wait at least one more minute. Flags take up to 30s, so instances can disagree for up to 30s after a change.
haiku-low.q4: It copies at most 2,000 rows per batch and sleeps whenever mysql_replica_lag_seconds is above 5.
haiku-low.q5: Reads move only after a full checker pass reports 0 mismatches. The source of truth moves after reads have been 100% on PG for 3 days and the last nightly checker run was clean.
haiku-low.q6: The users_pg_pending outbox table in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the change. The sweeper replays it into PG within about 15s, or once PG is back.
haiku-low.q7: Tombstones: deletes write the id to users_tombstones in both DBs, and safe copies skip tombstoned ids. Per-id locks stop a copy and a delete from interleaving.
haiku-low.q8: In users_backfill_progress in PG (one row: last_copied_id, target_max_id), updated in the same PG transaction as each batch. It stops when a read finds no rows at or below target_max_id.
haiku-low.q9: The checker compares both DBs 10,000 ids at a time, re-checks differences against the primary after 5s, and pushes remaining mismatches to the source-of-truth outbox for the sweeper to fix.
haiku-low.q10: Every instance must confirm frozen first, plus 5s, before cutover, so no instance writes MySQL-first while another writes PG-first. If not done by T0+60s, flip to dual_mysql_primary and retry another day.
haiku-low.q11: PG's identity assigns ids after cutover, restarted at MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT counter. After a rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to PG's next identity value so MySQL cannot reissue an id.
haiku-low.q12: MySQL gets every write via explicit-id safe copies that push AUTO_INCREMENT past them, with PG repair and nightly checks. Rollback: freeze, drain outbox, bump AUTO_INCREMENT, set dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg=0. It ends at pg_only, after 14+ days with a clean nightly pass.

sonnet.q1: MySQL first: one MySQL transaction does the change, reads the row back and upserts the users_pg_pending outbox row; commit means the write is done. Then a safe copy to PG with a 500 ms timeout, then the outbox row is removed if the token matches. If PG fails or times out, the caller does not see a failure; the request succeeds and the outbox row stays.
sonnet.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the existing row's version (also skipped if the id is in that DB's users_tombstones; inserted if the id is missing).
sonnet.q3: Every instance must be confirmed on dual_mysql_primary (via app_flag_value), and then at least another minute must pass. Instances can disagree for up to 30s after a flag change, since they refresh flags every 30s.
sonnet.q4: It reads from the MySQL replica rather than the primary, uses batches of at most 2,000 rows in id order, and sleeps whenever mysql_replica_lag_seconds > 5.
sonnet.q5: Reads move to PG only after the checker has done a full clean pass (0 mismatches), ramping read_from_pg 1, 10, 50, 100 with at least an hour at each level while PG errors and p99 stay within MySQL's. The source of truth moves (cutover) only after reads have been 100% on PG for at least 3 days and last night's checker run was clean, at a quiet time.
sonnet.q6: The users_pg_pending outbox row (user_id plus token, created_at), kept in MySQL, written in the same transaction as the user change so it survives a crash. The MySQL-side sweeper/catch-up worker (wakes every 10s, grabs rows older than 5s) re-reads the current row from the MySQL primary, safe-copies it to PG (or deletes in PG and adds a tombstone if the row is gone), then deletes the outbox row if the token is unchanged.
sonnet.q7: Every delete writes its id into users_tombstones in both DBs in the same transaction as removing the row; safe copy skips ids in the target's tombstones. A copy and a delete of one id can't interleave because both take a per-id lock first (pg_advisory_xact_lock(id) in PG, a locking read of the id in users_tombstones in MySQL).
sonnet.q8: In the PG table users_backfill_progress (one row: last_copied_id and target_max_id). last_copied_id is written in the same PG transaction as each batch, so a failed batch rolls back with its progress and a crash resumes from there. It stops when a read finds no rows left at or below target_max_id (max(id) read on the MySQL primary at start); newer ids are dual-written.
sonnet.q9: The checker (comparer) goes through both DBs 10,000 ids at a time comparing id, version and a hash of other columns, reading the MySQL replica (pausing while lag > 5s). It re-checks each difference against the source-of-truth primary 5s later, and pushes the ones that remain into the outbox in the source-of-truth DB (users_pg_pending before cutover), where the sweeper fixes them. It reports a mismatch count per pass.
sonnet.q10: The cutover first sets write_mode=frozen and waits until every instance shows frozen in app_flag_value (up to 30s) plus 5s for the write deadline, so no instance is writing MySQL-first while another writes PG-first. Then it waits for users_pg_pending to be empty, restarts the PG identity, and sets dual_pg_primary. If not finished by T0+60s, flip back to dual_mysql_primary (nothing to undo) and retry another day; total pause stays at or under 90s.
sonnet.q11: PG assigns new ids via its identity (BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY), restarted at n = MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT counter read on the primary, which is above every id ever issued (including erased ones in tombstones). After a rollback, MySQL's AUTO_INCREMENT is set to the PG identity's next value (ALTER TABLE users AUTO_INCREMENT = ...) so MySQL can't reissue an id PG gave out; also each MySQL copy with an explicit id drags AUTO_INCREMENT past it.
sonnet.q12: Each PG-primary write does a PG transaction including a users_mysql_pending upsert, then a safe copy to MySQL (500 ms timeout) and removes the outbox row if the token matches; on failure the PG-side repair worker fixes MySQL, and the nightly checker pushes mismatches to users_mysql_pending. Rollback (PG must be reachable, within 14+ days): freeze at a new T0 (frozen, confirmed, +5s), wait for users_mysql_pending to be empty, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to PG identity's next value, then set write_mode=dual_mysql_primary and read_from_pg=0; if not done by T0+60s, put back dual_pg_primary and retry later. The option ends at pg_only (retire MySQL, after at least 14 days since cutover with no rollback and a clean nightly pass), the point of no return; from the first pg_only write MySQL is missing data.
